anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used to format the dataset, not a paper describing this dataset.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a specification/standard extension of BIDS for EEG, which this dataset's BIDS organization follows; it does not describe this silent-reading dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Participants viewed words forming naturalistic stories, presented one at a time on a grey background with a central fixation cross, while EEG was recorded with BrainVision. Triggers mark word onsets in unique versus repeated stories, as well as run onset and run end. Preprocessed data are provided as per-channel arrays of words by time points.

citation_details.title: The Genus Aureobasidium From Sooty Mould Communities in Poland, Including A. epipinicola sp. nov. and A. insectorum , New to Europe
citation_details.author: Paweł Czachura, Marcin Piątek
citation_details.abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Aureobasidium contains numerous species inhabiting diverse habitats, including plants, where they live as saprobes, epiphytes, endophytes or pathogens. Sooty moulds are epiphytes forming multispecies communities on the surface of leaves or needles covered with exudates of some insects. On leaves and needles, they form black coatings and therefore have a negative impact on plants due to the reduction of photosynthesis and foliar gas exchange. Additionally, they decrease the visual aesthetic qualities of ornamental plants in urban environments. In temperate climates, sooty moulds were previously commonly assigned to the species Fumago vagans , which was proven to belong to two different species, Aureobasidium pullulans and Cladosporium herbarum . A. pullulans was indeed reported from sooty mould communities based on morphological features or using sequences of a single locus (ITS). In this study, 32 strains of Aureobasidium isolated from sooty mould communities covering leaves/needles of six ornamental woody plants from municipal greenery in Poland were subjected to multilocus (ITS, LSU, rpb2 , tef1 , tub2 ) phylogenetic analyses and morphological analyses in order to resolve their species assignment. Thirty strains were identified as A. pullulans but one strain belonged to an undescribed species A . epipinicola , and one strain was assigned to A . insectorum , a species recently described from China. This study confirms that A . pullulans is a constant inhabitant of sooty mould communities in temperate regions and reports that other Aureobasidium species may also be involved in this disease complex.

citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai C
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.
